title: Death's Five Pourings and the Twelve Dignities of Error
arc: The teaching traces how the cosmos of darkness was built up out of Death's own poured-forth corpses in five successive emanations, producing the five worlds of the flesh and the twelve spirits of error of the zodiac, all of which arose against the First Man and were finally humbled by him.
reading:
This chapter is a cosmogony in reverse: instead of describing how the heavens were built out of divine love and wisdom, it describes how the cosmos of self-love was constructed out of Death's own outpoured remains. The teaching opens by setting the scene against the Greatness and the hidden things of God — the two substances, light and darkness, divine and proprium. Within that frame the master narrates a sequence in which Death rises up to plant himself "unto eternity" out of the depth, and the entire structure of the lower cosmos is shown to be nothing other than his corpses arranged in ordered courses against the First Man.

The first kind is the inert state of darkness itself: those who are simply in the land of darkness, the original undifferentiated state of self-love before it has begun to bring forth. After a great time in which no glory was given — that is, in which no influx of divine acknowledgment animated this realm — Hyle gushes forth and pours upward. Her gushing yields the trees of death: perceptions whose root is the desire of death rather than the Mother of Life. This is the second kind. From these trees come, as the fourth kind, the bitter fruits — the works of life produced from corrupt perception, growing in the five trees that stand in the five worlds of darkness. The progression is the inverted mirror of the regenerative order: where divine generation moves seed → tree → sweet fruit, here Hyle's enthumesis of death moves outpouring → tree-of-death → bitter fruit.

In the fifth time Hyle spreads herself out unto her offspring, and the five worlds are molded — begotten from her five-fold structure as the five worlds of the flesh, the five creatures of darkness in whom Death stood fast. These are the discrete degrees of the proprium, the negative counterpart to the Five Storehouses of the First Man. The teaching insists on their fleshly character: they are the somatic register of evil, structured exactly as the human natural is structured, but in inversion. Within this fivefold body of darkness the male and female portions of each kind mingle in the middle — fire (corrupt love) with the desire of the flesh — and from this mingling the bodies of the worlds of darkness draw their nourishment from the five elements. What corresponds in the Light to the orderly conjunction of love and wisdom appears here as a churning of lust and concupiscence feeding itself.

Out of this fivefold body the chapter then opens onto the mystery of the twelve dignities. The twelve kinds that came-to-be in the darkness against the First Man are the twelve spirits of error, and these are identified with the twelve zodiac-signs. In correspondence, the zodiac is the cosmic circuit of natural states, the binding-wheel of the sphere; here the master is showing that this circuit, as it operates in the unredeemed cosmos, is the array of twelve falsities-from-evil set in battle-order against descending Divine Truth. The completeness-in-church that the number twelve normally signifies appears in its opposite sense: a complete encampment of error, the full articulation of the proprium across every aspect of natural life.

The closing note reverses the whole picture. All of this — the five kinds of death's outpouring, the molded worlds of flesh, the twelve dignities of error standing on their feet against him — is gathered up into a single statement: this is the manner in which the First Man humbled the Darkness. The narrative of the building-up of death's cosmos is thus told not as a triumph of Hyle but as the disclosure of what the descending Divine Human came to overcome. The teaching's spiritual point is therefore double: it shows the regenerating reader the actual anatomy of the proprium he carries — fivefold in its world-body, twelvefold in its array of false rationalities — and it shows that this entire ordered host, however eternally Death meant to plant himself, has already been pinned down by the First Man's descent. The cosmos of darkness is real as structure, but it is real only as that which has been humbled.

Several gaps obscure particulars (the third kind is not legible in the surviving line, and the precise wording of the twelve's painting and fixing is broken), but the fivefold sequence and the twelvefold zodiacal array are clear enough that the arc as a whole stands.

major_images.meaning: Self-love attempting to fix itself as a permanent cosmic principle in opposition to the Living

major_images.meaning: The corrupt matrix generating falsities from itself in five discrete degrees, the inverted counterpart of the Mother of Life

major_images.meaning: The fivefold complete body of the proprium — the discrete degrees of self-love as the negative of the Five Storehouses

major_images.meaning: The conjunction of corrupt love and concupiscence by which the worlds of darkness sustain themselves
